rule: Each entry is one limit the NSSCAS Biology 8223 syllabus states, with the pattern authoring checks scan learner-facing text for. The quoted sentence is the syllabus's; the pattern is our judgement of what teaching past the limit would look like. The build tools ignore applies_to and scan every topic with every pattern, so each pattern is written to be safe anywhere: it fires only on text that is past the limit. The controls are run when this file is built. Two limits are not scanned because no safe pattern exists: the sampling-method limit (objective 1.2-06 allows suitable methods) and the local-or-regional restoration examples; a reviewer reads for those, and for teaching past any limit by paraphrase.

entries.construct: species concepts other than the biological, morphological, ecological and behavioural concepts

source.quote: limited to the biological, morphological, ecological and behavioural concepts

must_catch: The phylogenetic species concept groups organisms by common ancestry.
Under the recognition species concept, organisms share a mate-recognition system.
must_allow: The biological species concept says a species can interbreed to produce fertile offspring.
The morphological concept uses observable structure.
Cohesion is the attraction between water molecules.

must_catch: Bacteria have mesosomes that carry out respiration.
A mesosome is an infolding of the cell membrane.
must_allow: Prokaryotic cells have no membrane-bound organelles.
The bacterial cell wall is made of peptidoglycan.

source.quote: no calculations involving water potential will be set

must_catch: Calculate the water potential of the solution using the solute potential.
Water potential = solute potential + pressure potential.
must_allow: Water moves from a higher to a lower water potential.
Place the tissue in sucrose solutions of different concentrations and find the concentration with no mass change.

entries.construct: solute potential, pressure potential and osmotic potential as terms

source.quote: Movement of water should be described in terms of water potential. Knowledge of solute potential is not expected

must_catch: The solute potential of the cell sap is negative.
Pressure potential rises as the cell becomes turgid.
must_allow: Water potential is the tendency of water to move.
A turgid cell has pushed against its wall.

entries.construct: roles of water beyond solvent action, specific heat capacity and latent heat of vaporisation
entries.pattern: \b(?:ice floats|ice is less dense|maximum density|surface tension)\b

source.quote: limited to solvent action, specific heat capacity and latent heat of vapourisation

must_catch: Ice floats because it is less dense than liquid water.
Surface tension lets insects walk on water.
must_allow: Water is a good solvent for ions and polar molecules.
Its high specific heat capacity buffers temperature changes.
Cohesion and tension in the xylem pull water upwards.

source.quote: details of the chloride shift are not required

must_catch: Chloride ions move into the red cell in the chloride shift.
The Hamburger shift keeps the cell electrically neutral.
must_allow: Carbonic anhydrase makes carbonic acid from carbon dioxide and water.
Hydrogen ions bind to haemoglobin, forming haemoglobinic acid.

entries.construct: nervous and hormonal control of the heart

source.quote: reference should be made to the sinoatrial node, the atrioventricular node and the Purkyne tissue, but not to nervous and hormonal control

must_catch: The vagus nerve slows the heart rate.
Adrenaline increases heart rate through the sympathetic nerves.
must_allow: The sinoatrial node sends waves of excitation across the atria.
Purkyne tissue carries the signal down the septum.
Acetylcholine is released by a neurone and binds to a receptor on the next cell.
Insulin acts on liver cells as a signalling molecule.

entries.construct: non-infectious disease examples other than sickle cell anaemia and lung cancer

source.quote: limited to sickle cell anaemia and lung cancer

must_catch: Diabetes is a non-infectious disease.
A non-infectious disease such as scurvy has a dietary cause.
must_allow: Sickle cell anaemia is a non-infectious disease caused by a gene mutation.
Lung cancer is a non-infectious disease.
Insulin acts on liver cells.

entries.construct: detailed life cycle of the malarial parasite

source.quote: a detailed study of the life cycle of the malarial parasite is not required

must_catch: Sporozoites enter the liver cells and divide.
Merozoites invade red blood cells.
must_allow: The female Anopheles mosquito transmits Plasmodium.
The parasite must develop in the mosquito before it can infect another person.

entries.construct: T-lymphocyte types other than T-helper and T-killer cells

source.quote: limited to T-helper cells and T-killer cells

must_catch: Regulatory T cells switch the response off.
Suppressor T cells dampen the response.
must_allow: T-helper cells stimulate B-lymphocytes.
T-killer cells destroy infected cells.
Memory cells give a faster secondary response.

entries.construct: chromosome structure beyond DNA, histone proteins, chromatids, centromere and telomeres

source.quote: limited to DNA, histone proteins, chromatids, centromere and telomeres

must_catch: The kinetochore attaches the chromosome to the spindle fibre.
DNA winds round histones to form nucleosomes.
must_allow: A chromosome has two chromatids joined at the centromere.
Telomeres are caps at the ends of the chromatids.
Spindle fibres attach to the centromere.

entries.construct: structural formulae of nucleotides and bases

must_catch: Draw the structural formula of adenine.
Guanine has the formula C5H5N5O.
must_allow: Adenine and guanine are purines with a double ring structure.
A nucleotide has a phosphate group, a pentose sugar and a nitrogenous base.
